THEY Choose Self-Preservation: The World.why: Morpheus is captured in the basement, converting him from leader to liability whose Zion codes will soon expire and establishing the tactical arithmetic where cutting losses preserves the crew.

Smith escalates to a doubled serum dosage that drives Morpheus's alpha pattern into an ordered wave — the sign he is about to break — pricing him as a lost asset and making abandonment the rational self-preservation answer.
The crew's survival protocol defaults to pulling Morpheus's plug and abandoning him rather than mounting a rescue, the cold calculus to cut losses that Neo must physically interrupt to stop.

When Sentinels arrive Morpheus immediately converts to preservation protocol — reading the radar, giving the crew minutes, ordering the EMP charged — applying the same self-preservation logic ship-wide and making sacrifice appear illogical.

I Choose Self-Sacrifice: Neo's Faith Wag.why: Morpheus pins an Agent and orders Trinity to get Neo out, giving his life so others escape (sc-115). Neo witnesses this self-sacrifice, creating an internal debt that makes later self-preservation cost his emerging self-respect.

Smith doubles the serum until Morpheus's alpha pattern orders into a wave, sign he will break (sc-144). For Neo this makes rescue tactically hopeless, so choosing to go anyway can only be an illogical faith wager on a man, not a calculation.

Neo physically stops the plug pull and commits to re-enter to save Morpheus while explicitly denying he is the One (sc-148). With no prophetic cover the rescue is pure self-sacrifice, a wager he cannot justify logically, only believe in.

Neo drops the helicopter, guns down Agents and leaps after the falling handcuffed Morpheus to catch him mid-air as Smith shoots (sc-165-169). He enacts the wager, risking his own life to honor the debt rather than preserve himself.

Alone before a dead escalator and urged by Trinity to run, Neo turns back to face the hunter and hardens into gunfighter calm (sc-179). He repeats the refusal to flee, proving the earlier wager was an internalized stance for self-sacrifice.

YOU Model Self-Sacrifice: Morpheus's Liv.why: Morpheus establishes the prophecy faith that frames Neo as the One worth any risk, declaring the search is over and committing to guide him, creating the ideological setup that makes his later self-sacrifice intelligible as modeling for Neo.
Morpheus directly models self-sacrifice by pinning an Agent and ordering Trinity to get Neo out, choosing to give his own life so the others escape, enacting the sacrifice horn for Neo to witness.

Captured and drugged with doubled serum driving his alpha pattern toward breaking, Morpheus spends his last agency fighting to keep his mind from cracking rather than saving himself by betraying Zion, refusing self-preservation through betrayal.

After Neo's illogical rescue succeeds, Morpheus reframes that wager as destiny, cutting off Neo's report and reinterpreting both prophecy and Trinity's silence as confirmation of the One, converting faith-wager into worldview where a man is worth any risk.

WE Choose Each Other: Neo and Trinity's.why: Inside the TV repair shop Neo breaks free of Trinity's embrace and sends her out first when the phone rings, enacting WE mutual protection that puts the other's survival before own escape.

Smith's doubled serum drives Morpheus's alpha pattern into an ordered wave as he fights to keep his mind from cracking, gutting Trinity and creating the shared grief WE must convert into joint action.

Trinity converts grief over Morpheus's condition and Neo's denial he is the One into command, insisting on directing the rescue on her terms and binding WE to a joint wager that rejects self-preservation.
Ripped back to the ship Trinity demands Tank send her back to Neo trapped with Smith, refusing to preserve herself while WE's other half remains in lethal danger.
After Smith shoots Neo and monitors flatline as the crew gives him up, Trinity refuses the survival verdict, takes hold of his body and kisses him, and WE revives him, defeating self-preservation.

In the darkened hovercraft Trinity keeps vigil as Neo wakes at her voice and reaches for her while she weeps and kisses him, confirming WE's loyalty endures beyond the survival logic that declared him lost.

WE (Crew) Split the Dilemma: Cypher's Se.why: Crew watches Neo's failed rooftop jump split between doubters and believers, making visible a community actively wrestling over whether faith in one man is worth dying for.
Cypher embodies self-preservation by recasting prophecy as a body count — five before Neo took on an Agent and died — then completes the horn by bargaining with Smith over steak to save himself.
Cypher covertly connects a phone and drops it in the alley garbage can, materially enabling the Agents to trace and trap the crew and carrying cynical accounting into active betrayal.
Cypher reaches the TV repair shop exit first, wakes on the ship and draws a concealed rifle, positioning to execute murder of crewmates for his own survival.
Cypher murders Apoc and Switch and delivers Morpheus to the Agents to save himself, completing self-preservation to its lethal end until surviving Tank strikes him down.
Survivors wake to count the sacrifice horn's price — Dozer dead, Tank wounded, Apoc and Switch gone — confirming believers pay with lives while self-preservation is stopped.

Neo and Trinity live the sacrifice horn Cypher rejected — storming the government building under certain death to extract Morpheus, with Neo leaping to catch his handcuffed body mid-fall rather than fleeing to save themselves.

Aboard the Nebuchadnezzar the crew watches together as Neo halts the Agents' volley and destroys Smith, Morpheus declaring him the One — communal vindication that the believers' costly sacrifice outweighed Cypher's self-preservation.
